analyst.summary: HG Infra Engineering has taken on substantially more debt to fund its road/HAM asset build-out - borrowings more than tripled in three years - while reported profit has actually declined and free cash flow has been negative for two consecutive years. The stock's modest valuation looks like fair pricing of this leverage and execution risk rather than a bargain, especially set against a broader slowdown visible across other road-EPC names. We recommend keeping this a Sell.
